what: Domain vocabulary (use these exact terms in plots, docs and messages)
title: CLAUDE.md — Rceattle
text: Match vocabulary axis labels, documentation, console messages; don’t substitute lay phrasing. Reference points: Amendment-56 SPR proxies — F40% = max FABC, F35% = FOFL, B40% = BMSY proxy (Tier 3); Tier 1 uses estimated FMSY/BMSY. Don’t write “MSY” SPR proxy meant. SSB = female spawning-stock biomass. “Recruitment deviations” (log-scale), “recruitment error”. Selectivity: name form — logistic / double-normal / gamma / nonparametric / semi-parametric. Don’t call every dome shape “double-normal”. Composition: age comps, length comps, conditional age--length (CAAL). ageing-error matrix applies age/CAAL data fit; length-stocks none. Data weighting: Francis (2011), McAllister–Ianelli, Dirichlet-multinomial. Diagnostics: Mohn’s rho (retrospective), OSA residuals, likelihood profiles.

title: 6. Building a data object in R
code: library(Rceattle)  # Define core dimensions up front, these drive the size of all downstream arrays. nspp     <- 2   # number of species (or stocks) nages    <- 10  # maximum age classes (same for all species here) nlengths <- 20  # number of length bins (for age-length keys / CAAL data) nyrs     <- 30  # number of hindcast years years    <- 1:nyrs  simData <- list()

title: 6. Building a data object in R
text: scalars vectors describe biological structure species control population model used.
code: simData$nspp    <- nspp simData$styr    <- 1       # first year of hindcast simData$endyr   <- nyrs    # last year of hindcast simData$projyr  <- nyrs + 10  # last year of the projection period  # Character labels shown in plots and output tables simData$spnames <- paste0("Species", 1:nspp)  # nsex: 1 = combined-sex model (male and female treated as one group), #        2 = sex-structured model (separate selectivity and mortality by sex) simData$nsex    <- rep(1, nspp)  # Calendar month of spawning, used to compute the fraction-of-year weight # applied to spawning stock biomass (e.g., 6 = mid-year spawning) simData$spawn_month <- rep(6, nspp)  simData$nages   <- rep(nages, nspp)   # number of age classes per species simData$minage  <- rep(1, nspp)       # minimum age (usually 1) simData$nlengths <- rep(nlengths, nspp)  # estDynamics controls how population abundance is estimated: #   0 = estimate population dynamics (standard statistical catch-at-age) #   1 = fix N-at-age exactly to values in NByageFixed (e.g., external estimates) #   2 = scale NByageFixed by a single estimated scalar per species simData$estDynamics <- rep(0, nspp)  # Indices linking each species to its weight and growth datasets. # Multiple weight schedules can exist (e.g., fleet-specific); these point to # which one is used for total biomass (pop) and spawning biomass (ssb). simData$pop_wt_index <- 1:nspp simData$ssb_wt_index <- 1:nspp simData$pop_age_transition_index <- rep(1, nspp)  # Length-weight relationship coefficients: W = alpha * L ^ beta. # Used internally to convert length-based selectivity to weight when estimating growth. simData$alpha_wt_len <- rep(0.00001, nspp) simData$beta_wt_len  <- rep(3, nspp)  # Prior or initial standard deviation for log-recruitment deviations. Controls the # strength of the recruitment penalty in penalized-likelihood mode. simData$sigma_rec <- rep(1, nspp)  # Non-modeled ("other") prey biomass available to predators. Used in # multi-species mode to prevent unrealistically high predation mortality when # modeled prey are scarce. Setting this too low forces predators to over-eat # modeled prey; too high dilutes the predation signal. simData$other_food <- rep(1e5, nspp)

title: 6. Building a data object in R
text: row defines one fleet (fishery survey) controls modeled. Multiple fleets can target species.
code: # Fleet_type: #   "Fishery", contributes catch and catch-at-age/length composition data #   "Survey", contributes an abundance index and composition data #   "Off", fleet is present in the data but excluded from the likelihood  # Selectivity options (Selectivity column), use the string name or integer code: #   "Fixed"              (0), fixed at values in emp_sel; not estimated #   "Logistic"           (1), two-parameter ascending logistic (a50, slope) #   "NonParametric"      (2), freely estimated selectivity-at-age/length with smoothness penalty #   "DoubleLogistic"     (3), ascending + descending dome-shaped logistic #   "DescendingLogistic" (4), descending logistic only (dome-shaped for oldest ages) #   "Hake"               (5), non-parametric selectivity à la Taylor et al. (Pacific hake) #   "2DAR1"              (6), 2D autoregressive random effects (bin × year) #   "3DAR1"              (7), 3D autoregressive random effects (bin × year × cohort) # # Selectivity_dimension: "Age" or "Length" #   Length-based selectivity requires an age-to-length transition matrix (see below).  # Catchability options (Catchability column), use the string name or integer code: #   "Fixed"                (0), Q fixed at Catchability_init; not estimated #   "Estimated"            (1), freely estimated on log scale #   "Estimated-with-prior" (2), estimated with a lognormal prior (Catchability_init, Catchability_prior_sd) #   "Analytical"           (3), Ludwig & Walters / Martell (1994) analytical Q #   "PowerEquation"        (4), power-equation Q (habitat area scaling) #   "Environmental"        (5), mu_q + X * beta, where X is a covariate in env_data #   "AR1"                  (6), REMOVED in 5.12.0; data_check() errors. Use a q #                                  linkage with ar1(1 | Year) and observe = <column> #   NA, not applicable (use for fisheries without CPUE)  # Comp_distribution / CAAL_distribution options: #   "Multinomial", standard multinomial #   "DirichletMultinomial", overdispersed; estimates a concentration parameter #   "MultinomialAFSC", AFSC variant of multinomial (marginal age + length)  simData$fleet_control <- data.frame(   Fleet_name  = paste0(c("Survey", "Fishery"),                        rep(paste(" Species", 1:nspp), each = 2)),   Fleet_code  = 1:(nspp * 2),       # unique integer ID per fleet   Fleet_type  = rep(c("Survey", "Fishery"), nspp),   Species     = rep(1:nspp, each = 2),   Month       = 0,                   # 0 = mid-year; calendar month otherwise    # Selectivity_index links fleets that share the same selectivity curve.   # Fleets with the same index share all selectivity parameters.   Selectivity_index         = 1:(nspp * 2),   Selectivity               = "Logistic",   Selectivity_dimension     = "Age",   N_sel_bins                = NA,    # used for NonParametric only   Sel_curve_pen1            = NA,    # smoothness penalty (NonParametric)   Sel_curve_pen2            = NA,   # Time_varying_sel:   #   0 / "Off" = time-invariant (default)   #   1 / "IID" = penalized log-normal deviates (SD fixed at Time_varying_sel_sd   #       unless random_sel = TRUE in fit_mod)   #   2 / "AR1" = REMOVED in 5.16.0; data_check() errors on it   #   3 / "Block" = time blocks (specify via R-side mapping)   #   4 / "RandomWalk" = random walk   #   5 / "RandomWalkAscending" = random walk on ascending portion of double logistic   Time_varying_sel          = 0,   Time_varying_sel_sd = 1,   Bin_first_selected        = 1,     # youngest fully-selected age or length bin   Sel_norm_bin             = "Off", # "Max", "Off", or a bin to normalize at   Sel_norm_bin_upper       = "Off", # "Off", or the top of a bin range   # Two-sex models only: whether the normalization reference is pooled over the   # sexes ("AcrossSexes", default, keeps relative sex selectivity) or taken per   # sex ("WithinSex", both sexes reach 1, only the shape differs).   Sel_norm_scope           = "AcrossSexes",    # Composition likelihoods   Comp_distribution = "Multinomial",   Comp_weights = 1,                  # input effective sample size multiplier   CAAL_distribution = "Multinomial",   CAAL_weights = 1,    # Index units and weight/growth linkage   Observation_units     = 1,          # 1 = weight (mt), 2 = numbers   Weight_index         = rep(1:nspp, each = 2),   Age_transition_index = 1,    # Catchability_index links fleets that share the same catchability parameter.   Catchability_index              = 1:(nspp * 2),   Catchability         = rep(c("Estimated", NA), nspp),   Catchability_init              = rep(c(1,   NA), nspp),   Catchability_prior_sd           = rep(c(0.2, NA), nspp),   # Time_varying_q:   #   0 / "Off" = time-invariant   #   1 / "IID" = penalized log-normal deviates (SD fixed at Time_varying_q_sd   #       unless random_q = TRUE in fit_mod)   #   2 / "AR1" = REMOVED in 5.16.0; data_check() errors on it   #   3 / "Block" = time blocks   #   4 / "RandomWalk" = random walk   Time_varying_q          = rep(c(0, NA), nspp),   Time_varying_q_sd = rep(c(1, NA), nspp),    # Estimate_index_sd:   #   0 = fix at Log_sd from index_data   #   1 = estimate a single SD   #   2 = analytical sigma (Ludwig & Walters 1994)   Estimate_index_sd  = rep(c(0,  NA), nspp),   Index_sd     = rep(c(1,  NA), nspp),    # Estimate_catch_sd:   #   0 = fix at Log_sd from catch_data (treats catch as known)   #   1 = estimate   #   2 = analytical sigma (Ludwig & Walters 1994); concentrates the sd out of   #       the catch likelihood, so catch stops pinning F as tightly   Estimate_catch_sd  = rep(c(NA, 0),  nspp),   Catch_sd     = rep(c(NA, 1),  nspp),    # Proj_F_proportion: how future F is distributed across fishery fleets per species.   # Must sum to 1 across fishery fleets for each species. NA for surveys.   Proj_F_proportion = rep(c(NA, 1), nspp) )

code: age_trans_list <- lapply(1:nspp, function(sp) {   tmp <- matrix(0, nrow = nages, ncol = nlengths)   diag(tmp[1:min(nages, nlengths), 1:min(nages, nlengths)]) <- 1   colnames(tmp) <- paste0("Length_", 1:nlengths)   cbind(data.frame(Age_transition_name  = paste("Species", sp),                    Age_transition_index = sp,                    Species              = sp,                    Sex                  = 0,                    Age                  = 1:nages), tmp) }) simData$age_trans_matrix <- do.call(rbind, age_trans_list)

what: 8. Multi-species bioenergetics parameters (optional in single-species mode)
title: 6. Building a data object in R
text: parameters govern Wisconsin bioenergetics model used compute predation mortality (M2) multi-species mode. single-species mode reach reported ration consumption_at_age, never objective, can omitted entirely; Rceattle fills missing scalars safe defaults (Ceq = 4, constant form reads environmental index). multi-species mode (msmMode > 0) Ceq, Cindex, Pvalue, fday, CA, CB, Qc, Tco, Tcm, Tcl, CK1, CK4 must supplied length-nspp vectors; data_check() list missing wrong-length. Likewise diet_data ration_data required. See ?build_M1 CEATTLE technical documentation full details parameter.
code: # Ceq: consumption (bioenergetics) equation form for each species: #   1 = Exponential (Stewart et al. 1983) #   2 = Warm-water temperature dependence (Kitchell et al. 1977) #   3 = Cool/cold-water temperature dependence (Thornton & Lessem 1979) #   4 = bypass bioenergetics; use ration_data directly (set CA = 1, fday = 1, CB = 0) simData$Ceq    <- rep(4,  nspp)  simData$Cindex <- rep(1,  nspp)   # which env_data covariate column drives it, counting from 1 simData$Pvalue <- rep(1,  nspp)   # proportion of maximum consumption realised simData$fday   <- rep(1,  nspp)   # foraging days per year  # Wisconsin model coefficients (CA, CB) and temperature dependence parameters simData$CA  <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$CB  <- rep(-1, nspp) simData$Qc  <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$Tco <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$Tcm <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$Tcl <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$CK1 <- rep(1,  nspp) simData$CK4 <- rep(1,  nspp)  # Diet composition likelihood for each predator species # 0 = Multinomial, 1 = Dirichlet-multinomial simData$Diet_distribution      <- rep(0, nspp) simData$Diet_comp_weights <- rep(1, nspp)  # Ration data (optional in single-species mode): observed mean ration-at-age from # bioenergetics studies. Required when msmMode > 0. Skip in single-species mode. # # When provided, columns are: Species, Sex, Year, Age1, ..., Age<nages>.  # Diet composition data: observed stomach content proportions (predator-prey pairs). # Required when msmMode > 0; skip in single-species mode. # # When provided, columns are: Pred, Prey, Pred_sex, Prey_sex, Pred_age, # Prey_age, Year, Sample_size, Stomach_proportion_by_weight.

code: plot_data(simData) # Key fit_mod() arguments: # # estimateMode: 0 = full fit (hindcast + projection) #               1 = hindcast only #               2 = projection only (fix parameters, run HCR) #               3 = evaluate only (MakeADFun, no optimisation), useful for debugging # # msmMode:      0 = single-species, 1 = Type II MSVPA, 2 = Type III MSVPA # # initMode:     0 = freely estimated initial N-at-age #               1 = equilibrium, F_init = 0, no init deviations #               2 = equilibrium, F_init = 0, with init deviations (default) #               3 = non-equilibrium: F_init estimated, init devs included #               4 = non-equilibrium: F_init scales R0 #               5 = equilibrium, F_init = 0, seeded by R_init displaced by the #                   year-1 recruitment deviation, no init deviations # # phase:        TRUE = use parameter phasing for improved convergence (recommended)  sim_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = simData,   estimateMode = 3,    # change to 0 for a real fit   msmMode      = 0,   initMode     = 2,   random_rec   = FALSE,   fit_control = fit_control(     phase        = TRUE,     verbose      = 1))

title: Environmental linkages and priors
text: Environmental drivers (temperature, prey density, climate indices) enter stock assessments recruitment, natural mortality, growth, catchability, selectivity. Rceattle exposes long-format linkage table: one row per estimated coefficient tying environmental term (user-specified design column) process parameter. Describe linkages linkage_spec(), formula-driven helper, pass result relevant build_*() function. process applies environmental offset linked parameter, year year. linkage path wired growth (von Bertalanffy Richards), natural mortality (M1), recruitment (R0, alpha, beta), catchability (q), selectivity (form’s parameters), , prior-, Dirichlet-multinomial composition weights.

what: A first example: temperature on K
title: Environmental linkages and priors
text: Suppose want sex- species-specific von Bertalanffy growth, von Bertalanffy K parameter responding temperature index species:
code: library(Rceattle) data(whamGrowthData) plot_data(whamGrowthData)  # Use logistic selectivity for all fleets in this example. whamGrowthData$fleet_control$Selectivity <- "Logistic" whamGrowthData$fleet_control$Selectivity_dimension <- "Length"  # 1. Attach an env_data table to the data list. Must include `Year` #    plus whatever covariates show up in your formulas. Here `temp` is #    a placeholder; in real use it would be a standardized SST series, #    PDO index, etc. yrs <- whamGrowthData$styr:whamGrowthData$endyr whamGrowthData$env_data <- data.frame(   Year = yrs,   temp = rnorm(length(yrs), 0, 0.1) )  # 2. Build a growth specification with one linkage per parameter that #    you want to vary. linkage_spec() captures (formula, by, link, #    init, bounds, priors) for one process parameter. growth_spec <- build_growth(   fun = "vonBertalanffy",   linkages = list(     K = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ temp,             # 2 columns: (Intercept) and `temp`       by      = ~ species + sex,    # one beta per (species, sex, column)       priors  = list(temp = normal(0, 0.1)) # Tight prior     )   ) )  # 3. Fit as usual. fit <- fit_mod(   data_list   = whamGrowthData,   growthFun   = growth_spec,   estimateMode = 0,    msmMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(verbose = 0) ) summary(fit)

title: Environmental linkages and priors
text: Key arguments (see ?linkage_spec full list): formula: one-sided R formula describing linear predictor (anything model.matrix() understands: ~ 1, ~ temp, ~ temp + PDO, ~ poly(temp, 2), factor predictors, etc.). param: target parameter name (e.g. "K"). Filled automatically spec registered linkages = list(K = ...) list key. : stratifying factors (default ~species); use ~species + sex per-(species, sex) coefficients, NULL share single coefficient set. species / sex / fleet: restrict spec specific strata. Use multi-spec form (Per-species / Per-sex formulas ) give different species, sexes, fleets different formulas. species fleet accept either 1-based ids model’s names (data_list$spnames / fleet_control$Fleet_name); sex accepts integers (1L, 2L) strings ("Females"/"Males", case-insensitive). Prefer names fleets: id wrong range attaches linkage different fleet model still fits, misspelled name errors lists fleets . link: relates linear predictor natural-scale target. "log" (default) gives multiplicative effect natural param; "identity" gives additive effect natural param. init / bounds: named lists keyed design-matrix column (init = list(temp = 0.05), bounds = list(temp = c(-2, 2))). priors: named list keyed design-matrix column. entry either Rceattle_prior list keyed species id; see Priors . re_group / est_phase: random-effects grouping (placeholder) estimation phase ordinal (0 fixes, 1+ estimates).
code: linkage_spec(   formula,   param     = NULL,   by        = ~ species,   species   = NULL,                 # ids or spnames   sex       = NULL,   fleet     = NULL,                 # Fleet_codes or Fleet_names   link      = "log",                # or "identity"   init      = NULL,   bounds    = NULL,   priors    = NULL,   re_group  = NA_character_,   est_phase = 1L )

(Intercept) rows prior evaluated natural scale (e.g. normal(0.3, 0.1) K means dnorm(K_natural, 0.3, 0.1)). Use lognormal(meanlog, sdlog) put normal directly log scale; default fit_control(bias_adjust_proc = TRUE) centred meanlog - sdlog^2/2, exp(meanlog) prior mean (median FALSE). covariate rows prior applies coefficient -, regardless link function. programmatic prior assembly (e.g. species-specific priors built loop) call prior_* constructors directly: prior’s negative log-density contributes Linkage-table priors row joint NLL:
code: prior_normal(mean, sd) prior_lognormal(meanlog, sdlog) prior_gamma(shape, rate) prior_beta(shape1, shape2) linkage_spec(   formula = ~ temp + PDO,   by      = ~ species,   priors  = list(     temp = normal(0, 1),     # informative, ~95% in (-2, 2)     PDO  = normal(0, 5)      # weak   ) ) priors <- lapply(species_specific_sds, function(s) prior_normal(0, s)) names(priors) <- c("temp", "PDO", "salinity") linkage_spec(formula = ~ temp + PDO + salinity, priors = priors) fit$quantities$jnll_comp["Linkage-table priors", ]

what: Putting a prior on the parameter itself
title: Environmental linkages and priors
text: Bayesian-style informative priors can applied directly base growth parameters (K, L1, Linf, m), natural mortality (M1), recruitment parameters (R0, alpha, beta). prior attached (Intercept) row re-targeted base parameter. syntax used column. pattern works linkage target, Linf, L1, m (Richards), M1, R0, alpha, beta. M1 intercept prior replaces build_M1(M1_use_prior = TRUE) species, fit_mod() refuses pair unless M2_use_prior = TRUE (prior total M).
code: # Example: prior on K for von Bertalanffy growth growth_spec <- build_growth(   fun = "vonBertalanffy",   linkages = list(     K = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,                              # intercept only, no env effects       by      = ~ species + sex,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 0.3),   # start at K = 0.3       # Use `lognormal(log(0.3), 0.1)` to get a normal prior on log(K).       priors  = list(`(Intercept)` = lognormal(log(0.3), 0.1))     )   ) )

title: Environmental linkages and priors
text: standard deviations length--age L1 Linf anchors (sd_L1, sd_Linf) exposed linkage targets , init / bounds / priors contract applies. act growth SD--age rather mean growth parameters, , SD--age year dimension, intercept-bearing formulas honored. Slope rows targets raise warning effect; slope-formulas (~ 0 + temp) error. can also key prior species id species- specific priors: prior contribution appears Linkage-table priors row joint negative log-likelihood: can inspect linked parameter values via linkage table, estimated slope coefficients, base-parameter array: approach works M1 want prior natural mortality : linkage prior applied verbatim, lognormal bias-correction term.
code: # Prior on the SD at L1 anchored at exp(log(5)) = 5 length units, # with a tight normal prior on the log scale. growth_spec_sd <- build_growth(   fun = "vonBertalanffy",   linkages = list(     sd_L1   = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species + sex,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 5),       # Prior on log-scale SD; switch to `normal(5, 0.3)`       # for a Normal on sd_L1.       priors  = list(`(Intercept)` = lognormal(log(5), 0.3))     ),     sd_Linf = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species + sex,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 15)     )   ) )  # After fit_mod(), the init values set the SD at L1 and the SD at Linf # (on the log scale), and the priors evaluate against those SD # parameters via the intercept re-targeting path described above. rec_spec <- build_srr(   srr_fun = 0,   linkages = list(     R0 = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 1000),       # Species-keyed priors on log-scale R0.       priors  = list(`(Intercept)` = list(         `1` = lognormal(log(1000), 0.2),         `2` = lognormal(log(1500), 0.3),         `3` = lognormal(log(800),  0.25)       ))     )   ) ) fit$quantities$jnll_comp["Linkage-table priors", ] fit$data_list$linkage_table[fit$data_list$linkage_table$param == "K", ] fit$estimated_params$beta_linkage          # (Intercept) rows are 0; slopes are estimated fit$estimated_params$log_growth_pars       # base K / L1 / Linf / m (on log scale internally) data("GOApollock") # Using GOA pollock as an example  # One-species model, lognormal(log(0.34), 0.01) prior on M1 # applied via the linkage intercept (equivalent to a Normal on log_M1). # The structural M1_model is kept at "sex_age_invariant" (= 1). M1_spec <- build_M1(   M1_model = "sex_age_invariant",   linkages = list(     M1 = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ 1,       by      = ~ species,       init    = list(`(Intercept)` = 0.34),       # Prior is on the natural-scale for M1.       # `lognormal(log(0.34), 0.01)` evaluates Normal on log(M1).       # Use `normal(0.34, 0.01)` for a Normal directly on natural M1.       priors  = list(`(Intercept)` = lognormal(log(0.34), 0.01))     )   ) )  # Fit the model - no manual mapping needed fit <- fit_mod(   data_list = GOApollock,   M1Fun     = M1_spec,   estimateMode = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(phase = TRUE) )

title: 2. HCRs and MSEs: an introduction
text: management strategy evaluation (MSE) runs management strategy closed loop: operating model (OM) represents “true” stock generates data, estimation model (EM) fitted data applies harvest control rule (HCR), resulting catch feeds back OM. example uses northern rockfish assessment OM.
code: library(Rceattle) data("NorthernRockfish2022") nrdata <- NorthernRockfish2022 nrdata$fleet_control$Proj_F_proportion <- 1  om <- Rceattle::fit_mod(   data_list = nrdata,   estimateMode = 0,  # Estimate   initMode = 1,      # Assume unfished equilibrium   M1Fun = build_M1(     M1_model = "sex_age_invariant",     linkages = list(       M1 = linkage_spec(         formula = ~ 1,         priors = list(           "(Intercept)" = lognormal(log(0.06), 0.05)         )       )     )   ),   fit_control = fit_control(phase = TRUE) )

title: 2. HCRs and MSEs: an introduction
text: HCR = build_hcr() argument fit_mod() sets harvest control rule biological reference points (BRPs). use NPFMC Tier 3 rule: fishing F40%, maxFABC rate (Amendment-56 SPR proxy FMSY), F35% overfishing limit (FOFL). B40% target, F ramped linearly, reaching zero spawning-stock biomass falls Alpha = 0.05 target. Plimit = 0.2 separate shutoff: fishing stops stock assessed overfished relative 20% unfished SSB. See ?build_hcr available rules reference points.
code: em <- Rceattle::fit_mod(   data_list = nrdata,   estimateMode = 0, # Estimate   initMode = 1,      # Assume unfished equilibrium   M1Fun = build_M1(     M1_model = "sex_age_invariant",     linkages = list(       M1 = linkage_spec(         formula = ~ 1,         priors = list(           "(Intercept)" = lognormal(log(0.06), 0.05)         )       )     )   ),   HCR = build_hcr(HCR = "NPFMC", # Tier3 HCR                   Ftarget = 0.4, # F40%                   Flimit = 0.35, # F35%                   Plimit = 0.2,  # No fishing when SB<SB20                   Alpha = 0.05),   fit_control = fit_control(verbose = 1, phase = TRUE) )

code: biennial <- seq(om$data_list$endyr + 2, om$data_list$projyr, by = 2) miss_yr  <- biennial[ceiling(length(biennial) / 3)]  mse6 <- run_mse(   om = om, em = em,   nsim = 10,   assessment_period = setdiff(biennial, miss_yr), # every year but miss_yr   sampling_period = c(1, 2) ) schedule <- setdiff(biennial, miss_yr)  # The years the missed assessment would have set: from the year after it, # through the next assessment that was completed. gap_yrs <- (miss_yr + 1):min(schedule[schedule > miss_yr])  # 10% reduction, held for exactly those years. buffer <- expand.grid(Year = gap_yrs, Species = seq_len(om$data_list$nspp)) buffer$mult <- 0.90  mse7 <- run_mse(   om = om, em = em,   nsim = 10,   assessment_period = schedule,   sampling_period = c(1, 2),   catch_mult = buffer )

title: 1. Rceattle: An Introduction
text: vignette fits sequence five single- multi-species models Rceattle, applied walleye pollock, arrowtooth flounder, Pacific cod Gulf Alaska eastern Bering Sea. model follows Holsman et al. (2016) Adams et al. (2022). Every function help available via ?. workflow : Install Rceattle Load Rceattle associated excel data Fit assessment models: model 1: single-species assessment model estimated recruitment estimated penalized effects; model 2: three single-species assessment models jointly estimated recruitment estimated penalized effects; model 3: model 2, natural mortality estimated species; model 4: model 3, recruitment estimated random effects; model 5: full multi-species assessment models time- age- varying natural mortality due predation. Compare models AIC Mohn’s rho (retrospective analysis) Review plots input data, diagnostics, results.

code: library(Rceattle)  data(BS2017SS) data(BS2017MS)  # Set the terminal projection year BS2017SS$projyr <- 2060 BS2017MS$projyr <- 2060  # Plot input data plot_data(BS2017SS)  # Fit baseline single- and multi-species models ss_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017SS,   inits        = NULL,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     phase        = TRUE,     verbose      = 1))  ms_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ss_run$estimated_params,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   niter        = 5,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,   suitMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))

title: 4. Projections and reference points
text: estimateMode = 2 runs projection period , holding estimated parameters fixed, specified harvest control rule. build_hcr(HCR = 2, Ftarget = ...) sets constant F species. several fisheries target species, Proj_F_proportion column fleet_control splits projected F across fleets. values must sum 1 per species.
code: BS2017MS$fleet_control$Proj_F_proportion <- 1  # One fishery fleet per species  ms_run_proj <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ms_run$estimated_params,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 2,   HCR          = build_hcr(HCR = "ConstantF",                             Ftarget = c(0.2342936, 0.513, 0.0774777)),   niter        = 5,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,   suitMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))  plot_catch(ms_run_proj, incl_proj = TRUE)

title: 4. Projections and reference points
text: Projection recruitment deviations live parameter list, can overwrite directly projecting. estimateMode = 3 evaluates model without re-estimating anything, updated deviations change projection.
code: nyrs      <- BS2017MS$endyr - BS2017MS$styr + 1 nyrs_proj <- BS2017MS$projyr - BS2017MS$styr + 1 yrs_proj  <- (nyrs + 1):nyrs_proj  # Replace future rec_devs with draws from N(0, 0.707) ms_run$estimated_params$rec_dev[, yrs_proj] <- stats::rnorm(   n    = length(ms_run$estimated_params$rec_dev[, yrs_proj]),   mean = 0,   sd   = 0.707 )  ms_run_proj2 <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ms_run$estimated_params,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 3,   # Evaluate only, do not re-estimate   niter        = 5,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,   suitMode     = 0,   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))

title: 4. Projections and reference points
text: Setting random_rec = TRUE treats log-recruitment deviations random effects, marginalized via Laplace approximation, rather penalized fixed effects. propagates recruitment process uncertainty projections.

title: 5. Single- vs. multi-species models
text: Single-species appropriate : Predation interactions unknown negligible species interest major predators prey system building initial model debugging data inputs Multi-species appropriate : Predation important source mortality (e.g., groundfish Bering Sea Gulf Alaska) want evaluate climate-driven changes predator prey abundance propagate food web Reference points account ecosystem effects common workflow fit single-species models first use estimates starting values (inits) multi-species run.

title: 5. Single- vs. multi-species models
text: niter argument controls many times population dynamics predation mortality equations iterated convergence within gradient step. Five iterations typically sufficient.
code: library(Rceattle)  # BS2017SS and BS2017MS use the same data structure but differ in M1_base: # the multi-species dataset has lower residual mortality because some of # that mortality is explained by predation (M2) in multi-species mode. data(BS2017SS) data(BS2017MS) BS2017SS$projyr <- 2060 BS2017MS$projyr <- 2060  plot_data(BS2017SS) # Single-species ss_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017SS,   inits        = NULL,   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 0, # <-- single-species   fit_control = fit_control(     phase        = TRUE,     verbose      = 1))  # Multi-species, start from single-species MLEs for stability ms_run <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017MS,   inits        = ss_run$estimated_params,  # warm start   file         = NULL,   estimateMode = 0,   niter        = 5,        # iterations between population and predation dynamics   random_rec   = FALSE,   msmMode      = 1,        # <-- Type II MSVPA   suitMode     = 0, # empirical suitability from diet data   fit_control = fit_control(     verbose      = 1))

what: Rceattle — Multispecies Stock Assessment in R
title: Rceattle — Multispecies Stock Assessment in R
text: Rceattle: R package fitting climate-linked, single- multi-species age-structured stock assessment models testing via diagnostics, simulation, management strategy evaluation. Rceattle implements models R using Template Model Builder (TMB; Kristensen et al., 2015). Data can supplied via bundled Excel template constructed programmatically R list (see Building data object without Excel vignette). Capabilities include: Single-species (msmMode = 0) multispecies (msmMode > 0) configurations, one- two-sex population dynamics One multiple stocks can fit jointly. Multiple fisheries surveys range catchability selectivity parameterizations (logistic, double-logistic, non-parametric, time-varying, etc) Stock–recruitment options (Beverton–Holt, Ricker, mean-recruitment, environmentally-driven) Estimable growth (von Bertalanffy / Richards/ empirical weight--age) Environmental linkages priors recruitment, natural mortality, growth parameters Bioenergetics-based predation input temperature-specific consumption (multispecies mode) Forward projections alternative harvest control rules climate scenarios Closed-loop MSE, retrospective, jitter, simulation testing Tidy outputs via S3 methods (.data.frame, coef, logLik, vcov, residuals, plot) See browseVignettes("Rceattle") package website full documentation. Installation operational / management use, pin specific tagged release rather tracking main, e.g.: maintainer email DESCRIPTION (grant.adams@noaa.gov) preferred contact questions package; please open issue bug reports feature requests discussion publicly searchable. Getting started 1-species model Fit 2018 Gulf Alaska pollock model, inspect fit, plot : 3-species model Fit three single-species model jointly Bering Sea data: multispecies model, set msmMode = 1. See package vignettes (browseVignettes("Rceattle")) projections, alternative harvest control rules, MSE testing, model diagnostics, non-Excel data construction. deeper context, see onboarding document Wiki. model can updated following instructions . Examples Additional code function examples using data Bering Sea Gulf Alaska groundfish applications can found examples folder include: * Fitting single-species models * Fitting multi-species models * Estimating growth * Alternative HCRs MSE testing * Simulation * Model diagnostics References Adams, G.D., Holsman, K.K., Barbeaux, S.J., Dorn, M.W., Ianelli, J.N., Spies, ., Stewart, .J., Punt, .E., 2022. ensemble approach understand predation mortality groundfish Gulf Alaska. Fish. Res. 251, 106303. doi:10.1016/j.fishres.2022.106303 Holsman, K. K., Ianelli, J., Aydin, K., Punt, . E., & Moffitt, E. . (2016). comparison fisheries biological reference points estimated temperature-specific multi-species single-species climate-enhanced stock assessment models. Deep Sea Research Part II: Topical Studies Oceanography, 134, 360-378. Kristensen, K., Nielsen, ., Berg, C. W., Skaug, H., & Bell, B. (2015). TMB: automatic differentiation Laplace approximation. arXiv preprint arXiv:1509.00660. Wassermann, S. N., Adams, G. D., Haltuch, M. ., Kaplan, . C., Marshall, K. N., & Punt, . E. (2025). code: # Rceattle (pulls CRAN dependencies automatically) install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("afsc-assessments/Rceattle")  # Optional: TMBhelper provides richer optimization diagnostics. # Rceattle falls back to plain nlminb + sdreport if it's not installed. # remotes::install_github("kaskr/TMB_contrib_R/TMBhelper") remotes::install_github("afsc-assessments/Rceattle@5.45.1") library(Rceattle)  # Gulf of Alaska pollock data (1977-2018) data(GOApollock) plot_data(GOApollock)  # Fit the hindcast fit <- fit_mod(   data_list    = GOApollock,   estimateMode = 0,                              # 0 = fit hindcast + projection   fit_control  = fit_control(phase = TRUE)       # optimizer / sdreport / phasing knobs )  # S3 methods: the fit behaves like an R model object fit                       # compact print summary(fit)              # same compact summary coef(fit)                 # estimated fixed-effect parameters logLik(fit)               # logLik with df attribute (AIC works) AIC(fit) vcov(fit)                 # fixed-effect covariance from sdreport as.data.frame(fit)        # return data.frame of derived quantities  # Plot dispatcher: pick a panel with `what` plot(fit, what = "biomass") plot(fit, what = "ssb") plot(fit, what = "recruitment") plot(fit, what = "index")  # Residuals across data sources (long-format data frame) ix_resid   <- residuals(fit, source = "index")                  # response (log-scale) index residuals comp_resid <- residuals(fit, type = "pearson", source = "comp") # Pearson composition residuals all_resid  <- residuals(fit)                                    # response residuals, all data sources library(Rceattle)  # Bundled Eastern Bering Sea single-species data (1979-2017) data(BS2017SS) plot_data(BS2017SS)  # Fit the hindcast (single-species mode) fit <- fit_mod(   data_list    = BS2017SS,   msmMode      = 0,                              # 0 = single-species   estimateMode = 0,                              # 0 = fit hindcast + projection   fit_control  = fit_control(phase = TRUE)       # optimizer / sdreport / phasing knobs )  # S3 methods: the fit behaves like an R model object fit                       # compact print summary(fit)              # same compact summary coef(fit)                 # estimated fixed-effect parameters logLik(fit)               # logLik with df attribute (AIC works) AIC(fit) vcov(fit)                 # fixed-effect covariance from sdreport as.data.frame(fit)        # return data.frame of derived quantities  # Plot dispatcher: pick a panel with `what` plot(fit, what = "biomass") plot(fit, what = "ssb") plot(fit, what = "recruitment") plot(fit, what = "index")  # Residuals across data sources (long-format data frame) ix_resid   <- residuals(fit, source = "index")                  # response (log-scale) index residuals comp_resid <- residuals(fit, type = "pearson", source = "comp") # Pearson composition residuals all_resid  <- residuals(fit)                                    # response residuals, all data sources

what: Rceattle: Fits the Multispecies Assessment Model (CEATTLE) Using TMB — Rceattle-package
title: Rceattle: Fits the Multispecies Assessment Model (CEATTLE) Using TMB — Rceattle-package
text: Implements CEATTLE model using Template Model Builder ('TMB'; Kristensen et al. 2015), can installed following https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/wiki/Download. Structured similar original manuscript terms modularization. Separate functions estimate retrospective temperature- size-specific predator rations, prey preference, weight--age. used inputs CEATTLE model evaluate predation mortality, recruitment, survival three target species change historical climate conditions harvest rates.

title: Specify the residual natural mortality (M1) model for Rceattle — build_M1
text: M1_model Vector scalar specifying M1 structural fixed- effects model. Either integer code equivalent string alias (forms accepted; integer code canonical): 0 / "fixed", use input M1_base (estimation). 1 / "sex_age_invariant", estimate one M1_{spp}. 2 / "sex_specific", estimate M1_{spp, sex}. 3 / "sex_age_specific", estimate M1_{spp, sex, age}. 4, 5, soft-deprecated env-driven codes; use linkages argument instead. See vignette("environmental-linkages--priors"). M1_re Vector scalar specifying M1 random-effects model. Either integer code equivalent string alias: 0 / "none", 1 / "iid_age", 2 / "iid_year", 3 / "iid_age_year", 4 / "ar1_age", 5 / "ar1_year", 6 / "ar1_age_year". updateM1 using initial parameters, use M1 fixed effects data (M1_base) instead. Default FALSE. M1_use_prior Vector scalar; TRUE M2_use_prior FALSE, apply lognormal M_prior / M_prior_sd M1 directly, refused alongside prior species' M1 linkage intercept. M2_use_prior Vector scalar; TRUE, apply lognormal prior M1 + M2 multi-species models. M_prior Natural-scale mean lognormal prior M (median bias_adjust_proc = FALSE). M_prior_sd SD (log-scale) lognormal prior M. M1_indices Soft-deprecated. Vector column indices env_data (excluding Year) environmentally linked M1 M1_model %% c(4, 5). Use linkages argument instead; see vignette("environmental-linkages--priors"). linkages Optional named list linkage_spec() objects keyed M parameter name (currently valid key "M1"). spec describes M1 depends environmental covariates stratifying factors (species, sex, age). offset enters additively (log scale) inside M1_at_age compute. row's age_bin == NA broadcasts offset across ages; specific values pin age slice.

title: Specify the growth model for Rceattle — build_growth
text: fun Growth function. Either string (GROWTH_FUNS: "empirical" (default), "vonBertalanffy", "Richards") equivalent integer code (0, 1, 2). canonical string form stored returned object. growth_age_L1 Von Bertalanffy / Richards anchor age (age mean length equals L1). Matches SS3's Growth_Age_for_L1 control input. Scalar (recycled across species) length-nspp vector per-species values. Default NA inherits data_list$growth_age_L1 supplied (e.g. SS3 converter), otherwise falls back max(0.5, minage[sp]) minage >= 1 models stay backwards-compatible minage = 0 models pick SS3-consistent half-year anchor. sd_plus_group oldest age class's SD--age treated (affects estimated growth, fun != "empirical"). "WHAM" pins plus-group SD upper anchor exp(sd_Linf) (WHAM SDAA convention); "SS3" instead interpolates length like interior age. Accepts string integer code (1/2), scalar length-nspp vector. Default NA inherits data_list$growth_sd_style present (refit keeps original choice), otherwise "WHAM". linkages Optional named list linkage_spec() objects keyed parameter name (must one GROWTH_LINKAGE_PARAMS). mean-growth keys (K, L1, Linf, m) accept arbitrary one-sided formulas make growth parameter year-varying (per-year offset around mean). SD-endpoint keys (sd_L1, sd_Linf) honor intercept-bearing formulas (typically ~ 1), thread init, bounds, priors onto growth SD--age, giving SDs prior/fix/initial-value contract mean parameters. Slope rows SD specs raise warning effect; slope-formulas (~ 0 + temp) error.

title: Specify the harvest control rule (HCR) used for Rceattle — build_hcr
text: HCR Harvest control rule use. Accepts integer equivalent string alias. Default = 0. See Details full list available options. DynamicHCR TRUE/FALSE. Whether use static dynamic reference points (default = FALSE). Ftarget Target fishing mortality rate (yr^-1) (SPR depletion based) input F projections. example, Ftarget spr F40%, enter 0.40. Flimit Limit fishing mortality rate (yr^-1) (SPR depletion based). example, Flimit spr F35%, enter 0.35. Ptarget Target spawning-stock biomass percentage static dynamic spawning-stock-biomass F = 0 (accounts recruitment). Plimit Limit spawning-stock biomass percentage static dynamic spawning-stock-biomass F = 0 (accounts recruitment). Alpha Parameter used NPFMC Tier 3 HCR. Pstar Quantile used uncertainty buffer given Flimit Sigma. Sigma Standard deviation used normally distributed uncertainty buffer given Flimit Pstar. Fmult Multiplier target F (default = 1). Used scale target fishing mortality following NEFSC convention. HCRorder multi-species models, order project fishing (e.g., predators first, prey).

title: Specify the harvest control rule (HCR) used for Rceattle — build_hcr
text: list containing harvest control rule associated biological reference points.

title: Specify the harvest control rule (HCR) used for Rceattle — build_hcr
text: Harvest control rule formulations currently implemented Rceattle: hcr = 0 "NoFishing": catch. Estimate hindcast. hcr = 1 "CMSY": CMSY. Maximize catch across species simultaneously. CMSY can constrained depletion fall Plimit. hcr = 2 "ConstantF": Constant input F set Ftarget species (vector single F). SPR (single-species ) based Flimit specified via Flimit. hcr = 3 "ConstantFSSB": F achieves Ftarget% SSB0 end projection. hcr = 4 "ConstantFSPR": Constant Fspr set Ftarget species. Can multiplied Fmult following NEFSC. hcr = 5 "NPFMC": North Pacific Fishery Management Council (NPFMC) Tier 3 spawner-per-recruit-based harvest control rule: Stock status: \(SB > SB Ftarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget$$ Stock status: \(Alpha < SB / SB Ftarget \le 1\) $$Fofl = Flimit * (SB / SB_{Ftarget} - Alpha) / (1 - Alpha)$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget * (SB / SB_{Ftarget} - Alpha) / (1 - Alpha)$$ Stock status: \(SB / SB Ftarget \le Alpha\) \(SB < Plimit * SB0\) $$Fofl = 0$$ $$Fuse = 0$$ hcr = 6 "PFMC": HCR based Pacific Fishery Management Council (PFMC) category 1 40-10 annual catch limit (ABC) harvest control rule assuming Fofl normally distributed standard deviation (sigma) = 0.5 uncertainty quantile buffer (P*) 0.45 (PFMC 2020). model uses Fspr single-species F achieves X% SSB0 multi-species. uncertainty buffer normal quantile function qnorm(Pstar, mean, Sigma); note qnorm(Pstar, Flimit, Sigma) = Flimit + qnorm(Pstar, 0, Sigma) – F Flimit \(Pstar < 0.5\). taper runs \(SB0 * Plimit\) \(SB0 * Ptarget\), 40-10 shape requires Ptarget = 0.40 Plimit = 0.10; default Plimit = 0 gives 40-0 rule. Target biological reference points : Stock status: \(SB > SB0 * Ptarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = qnorm(Pstar, Flimit, Sigma)$$ Stock status: \(SB0 * Plimit < SB \le SB0 * Ptarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = qnorm(Pstar, Flimit, Sigma) * \frac{SB0 * Ptarget * (SB - SB0 * Plimit)}{SB * SB0 * (Ptarget - Plimit)}$$ Stock status: \(SB < SB0 * Plimit\) $$Fofl = 0$$ $$Fuse = 0$$ hcr = 7 "SESSF": HCR based Southern Eastern Scalefish Shark Fishery (SESSF) spawner-per-recruit-based Tier 1 harvest control rule F_Limit=F_(20%), B_Limit=SB_20, F_Target (AFMA 2017) calculated follows: Stock status: \(SB > SB0 * Ptarget\) $$Fofl = Flimit$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget$$ Stock status: \(SB0 * Ptarget > SB > SB0 * Plimit\) $$Fofl = Flimit * (SB / (SB0 * Plimit) - 1)$$ $$Fuse = Ftarget * (SB / (SB0 * Plimit) - 1)$$ Stock status: \(SB < SB0 * Plimit\) $$Fofl = 0$$ $$Fuse = 0$$ NOTE: HCRs 0, 1, 2, 3, 6 work multi-species mode.

title: Specify the harvest control rule (HCR) used for Rceattle — build_hcr
code: # Tier 3 NPFMC control rule: F40% as FABC, F35% as FOFL. build_hcr(HCR = "NPFMC", DynamicHCR = FALSE, Ftarget = 0.4, Flimit = 0.35) #> $HCR #> [1] "NPFMC" #>  #> $DynamicHCR #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $Ftarget #> [1] 0.4 #>  #> $Flimit #> [1] 0.35 #>  #> $Ptarget #> [1] 0.4 #>  #> $Plimit #> [1] 0 #>  #> $Alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $Pstar #> [1] 0.45 #>  #> $Sigma #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $Fmult #> [1] 1 #>  #> $HCRorder #> [1] 1 #>   # No fishing: the projection a B0 reference point is read from. build_hcr(HCR = "NoFishing") #> $HCR #> [1] "NoFishing" #>  #> $DynamicHCR #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $Ftarget #> [1] 0.4 #>  #> $Flimit #> [1] 0.35 #>  #> $Ptarget #> [1] 0.4 #>  #> $Plimit #> [1] 0 #>  #> $Alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $Pstar #> [1] 0.45 #>  #> $Sigma #> [1] 0.5 #>  #> $Fmult #> [1] 1 #>  #> $HCRorder #> [1] 1 #>

Use analytic gradient phasing. Default TRUE. rel_tol Numeric tolerance used flag discontinuous likelihood warnings, comparing nlminb's objective fresh evaluation object came . May NULL spec built inside build_*() call infers parameter name enclosing list key (see build_growth()). data Optional data frame formula validation; validation performed fit time inside fit_mod(). one-sided formula naming stratifying factors get coefficients. Allowed names species, sex, age_bin, fleet (fleet catchability selectivity linkages). omitted, defaults base stratum whichever process spec attached , ~fleet catchability, selectivity, fleet composition weights (theta_comp / theta_caal), ~species recruitment, M, growth, diet weight (theta_diet), rarely need spell base case. Pass explicitly override: e.g. ~species + sex per-(species, sex) coefficients, NULL share single coefficient across every stratum. explicit (including NULL) always kept given. species optional vector species spec applies , given either 1-based species ids (c(1L, 2L)) species names matching data_list$spnames (c("Pollock", "Cod")). Names matched exactly, trimming whitespace, model assembled fit_mod(); unrecognized name error lists model's species. Give ids names, mix, R coerces c(1, "Cod") c("1", "Cod"). NULL (default) means every species strata$species materialization time. Use give different species different formulas, e.g. registering multiple specs parameter, see build_growth() multi-spec syntax. sex optional vector sex ids spec applies . May supplied integers (1L = female, 2L = male) character strings ("Females"/"Males", case-insensitive; "female", "male", "f", "m" also accepted). NULL (default) means every sex strata$sex materialization time. must include sex apply; otherwise warns effect. Use register separate specs per sex (e.g. one prior females, another males) parameter. fleet optional vector fleets spec applies , given either 1-based Fleet_codes (c(1L, 3L)) fleet names matching fleet_control$Fleet_name (c("Shelikof", "Summer BT")). Names matched exactly, trimming whitespace, model assembled fit_mod(); unrecognized name, one unique fleet_control, error lists model's fleets. Prefer names: Fleet_code wrong range attaches linkage different fleet still fits, whereas misspelled name . Give ids names, mix, R coerces c(7, "Pollock") c("7", "Pollock"). NULL (default) means every fleet strata$fleet materialization time. must include fleet apply; otherwise warns effect. Used catchability selectivity linkages give different fleets different formulas. link link function relating linear predictor natural-scale target parameter. One "log" (default) "identity". link = "log", log(param) = X * beta, slope contributions multiplicative natural-scale parameter. link = "identity", param = X * beta, slope contributions additive natural scale. linkage targets estimated log scale, "log" default. init optional named list initial values keyed design-matrix column name (e.g. list(`(Intercept)` = 4, temp = 0)), intercept parameter's natural scale slope link scale; missing entries default 0. bounds optional named list c(lower, upper) keyed way init. priors optional named list Rceattle_priors objects, keyed design-matrix column name. Inside argument may write normal(), lognormal(), gamma(), beta() directly, e.g. priors = list(temp = normal(0, 1)), equivalent priors = list(temp = prior_normal(0, 1)). re_group optional character: name random-effect grouping coefficients. NA (default) means fixed. est_phase optional integer estimation phase. Default 1L; 0 fixes coefficient init, holds inits given fit_mod() (estimated intercept's init starting value, inits win). Applies fixed-effect rows , coefficients beta_linkage. random-effect term's deviations held separate vector est_phase reach, est_phase < 1 formula containing one error rather silent -op; drop term, fix small SD via init = list(sigma = ), remove time variation. Values 1 currently inert every linkage row. observe optional character: ar1(1 | group) term, name env_data column measures AR1 latent (state-space covariate, sensu Rogers et al. 2024). latent enters linked parameter estimated effect size observed column. NULL (default) leaves AR1 plain random effect. latent zero-mean (estimated level), standardize observed covariate mean 0; non-zero-mean column confounds level intercept warns. obs_sd optional positive numeric: measurement SD observe covariate (one per observed group). Required observe, unused otherwise. Held fixed value default (obs_sd_est = FALSE); starting value obs_sd_est = TRUE. obs_sd_est optional single TRUE/FALSE (default FALSE): estimate observe measurement SD instead holding fixed, state-space survey-catchability (GOA pollock) model . Caveat: effect size obs_sd jointly identified observed covariate informative; smooth series AR1 latent can track exactly freely-estimated obs_sd collapses toward 0. Keep fixed unless covariate informative. used observe. integrate single TRUE/FALSE (default TRUE): whether random effect's deviations integrated Laplace approximation. integrate = FALSE instead estimates penalized fixed effect, deviations stay objective plain penalty reported standard errors like fixed effect. reproduces ADMB/AMAK convention behind legacy Time_varying_sel / Time_varying_q switches, Laplace-integrated rw() match (marginal likelihood holds log-determinant term penalized form counterpart ). title: Capture a linkage specification — linkage_spec
code: # A covariate on a growth parameter, one coefficient per species. Attach to a # parametric build_growth(); the default "empirical" form consumes no linkages. linkage_spec(~ temp, param = "K") #> <Rceattle linkage spec> #>   param:   K #>   formula: ~temp #>   link:    log  # A covariate on catchability for one fleet, named rather than numbered. # `by` defaults to ~ fleet for catchability, so it need not be given. linkage_spec(~ temp, fleet = "Pollock_survey_1_shelikof_acoustic") #> <Rceattle linkage spec> #>   param:   NA #>   formula: ~temp #>   fleet:   Pollock_survey_1_shelikof_acoustic #>   link:    log  # A separate coefficient per year, the fixed-effect alternative to rw()/ar1(). linkage_spec(~ factor(Year), fleet = "Pollock_survey_1_shelikof_acoustic") #> <Rceattle linkage spec> #>   param:   NA #>   formula: ~factor(Year) #>   fleet:   Pollock_survey_1_shelikof_acoustic #>   link:    log  # IID annual deviations; rw() for a random walk, ar1() for AR1. linkage_spec(~ (1 | Year)) #> <Rceattle linkage spec> #>   param:   NA #>   formula: ~(1 | Year) #>   link:    log  # A random walk estimated as a penalized fixed effect, which requires a # fixed SD, the ADMB/AMAK convention behind the legacy Time_varying_* # switches. linkage_spec(~ rw(1 | Year), init = list(sigma = 0.05), integrate = FALSE) #> <Rceattle linkage spec> #>   param:   NA #>   formula: ~rw(1 | Year) #>   link:    log #>   estimate: penalized fixed effect (integrate = FALSE)  # Intercept-only: a prior on the base parameter itself. The bare normal() # resolves to prior_normal() inside `priors`. linkage_spec(~ 1, priors = list(`(Intercept)` = normal(0, 1))) #> <Rceattle linkage spec> #>   param:   NA #>   formula: ~1 #>   prior:    (Intercept) ~ normal(0, 1) #>   link:    log

title: Plot composition fits and residuals — plot_comp
text: Diagnostic plots age / length composition data fitted Rceattle model, drawn ggplot2 consistent look plot.rceattle_osa(). default residual_type = "pearson" three figures produced per fleet x composition type: Pearson residual bubbles year bin, faceted fleet (, joint-sex data, sex); red = positive, blue = negative, sized magnitude. Pearson residual form used residuals.Rceattle(), standardized variance fleet's likelihood assumes, weight column Dirichlet-multinomial overdispersion already denominator. Annual composition: observed (shaded area) vs fitted (line) proportion age / length, one panel per year. Joint-sex data mirrored (females , males ). Aggregated composition: observed vs fitted, counts pooled fitted hindcast years. interval holds 95% data model predicts (confidence interval mean), observations outside indicate misfit. Poor expected count 10, slightly narrow throughout, treats fitted proportions known rather estimated data. shaded area fitted line span observed bins (extend past first/last bin), bins zero observed proportion retained (NA bins dropped), curves interpolated across gaps.

Supported processes deviations: "recruitment" rec_dev, prior N(-bias_adjust_proc * R_sd^2/2, R_sd^2) per species. "initial" init_dev, prior N(-bias_adjust_proc * R_sd^2/2, R_sd^2) per species. "catchability" index_q_dev, prior N(0, q_dev_sd^2) per index. "" returns every supported process present fit. Selectivity natural-mortality deviations (use random-walk / 2D-AR1 priors) yet supported. E.g. list(c(1, 2, 1)) fixes log_M1[1, 2, 1]; list(c(1, 1, 1), c(1, 2, 1)) fixes sex cells males-vs-females cross-profile species 1; list(1, 2) param = "sigmaR" cross-profiles species 1 2. omitted, defaults single species-1 slot shaped match resolved parameter (e.g. list(1) R_log_sd, list(c(1, 1, 1)) log_M1, list(1) rec_pars aliases) emits warning; pass slots explicitly silence warning. Defaulting requires length(values) == 1L (otherwise user must explicitly say cell grid targets). values list numeric vectors, one per entry slots. full grid fits expand.grid(values), single slot gives 1-D profile k slots give k-D cross-profile. transform map user values onto internal parameter scale substituting inits. Forwarding for now. #> `age_trans_matrix` data does not span range of age for species 1 will fill with 0s  # 1-D profile of sigmaR for species 1 (alias form, natural scale) p1 <- profile(ss_run,     param  = "sigmaR",     slots  = list(1),     values = list(seq(0.1, 1.5, by = 0.1)))  # Equivalent raw form (log scale, user does the transform) p1_raw <- profile(ss_run,     param     = "R_log_sd",     slots     = list(1),     values    = list(log(seq(0.1, 1.5, by = 0.1))),     transform = "identity")  # 2-D cross-profile of M1 across species 1 and 2 (sex 1, age 1). # BS2017SS is single-sex; with a multi-sex model the same form # (e.g. c(1, 1, 1), c(1, 2, 1)) would cross-profile males vs females. p2 <- profile(ss_run,     param  = "M1",     slots  = list(c(1, 1, 1), c(2, 1, 1)),     values = list(seq(0.1, 0.4, length.out = 3),                   seq(0.1, 0.4, length.out = 3)))  # 1-D profile of SRR alpha for species 1 (alias drops the rec_pars column) p3 <- profile(ss_run,     param  = "alpha",     slots  = list(1),     values = list(seq(2, 80, length.out = 20)))  # An empirical age-based M, moved as a whole. One slot per age bin of # species 1, all on ONE grid of multipliers, so the shape of the schedule is # preserved and 1 is the fitted model. Ages run minage .. minage + nages - 1. sp <- 1 p4 <- profile(ss_run,     param  = "M1",     slots  = lapply(seq_len(ss_run$data_list$nages[sp]),                     function(a) c(sp, 1, a)),     values = list(seq(0.6, 1.4, by = 0.05)),     joint  = "multiply")  # The same schedule shifted by a constant instead of scaled; 0 is the fit. p5 <- profile(ss_run,     param  = "M1",     slots  = lapply(seq_len(ss_run$data_list$nages[sp]),                     function(a) c(sp, 1, a)),     values = list(seq(-0.1, 0.1, by = 0.02)),     joint  = "add")  # Base catchability for a fleet, named rather than counted. If it shares a # Catchability_index the whole group moves with it. p6 <- profile(ss_run,     param  = "q",     slots  = list("BT_Pollock"),     values = list(seq(0.5, 2.0, by = 0.1))) # }

title: Residuals from an Rceattle fit — residuals.Rceattle
text: Residual kinds (type): "response" Observed minus fitted. index / catch log scale default (matching lognormal likelihood; set scale = "natural" arithmetic difference); comp / caal difference proportions, observed minus fitted. what: Environmental linkages: a unified, formula-driven API
title: Rceattle 4.1.0
text: new long-format linkage table lets users express process parameters depend environmental covariates stratifying factors (species, sex, age) single formula-driven helper, linkage_spec(). row table corresponds exactly one estimated coefficient. fit_mod() pools every spec shared design matrix X per-row parameter vector beta_linkage; TMB template iterates table accumulates per-process offsets linear predictor underlying parameter. New constructor: linkage_spec(). Captures (formula, , species, link, init, bounds, priors, est_phase) one process parameter. Anything model.matrix() understands works: ~ 1, ~ temp + PDO, ~ poly(temp, 4), ~ (temp^2), ~ splines::ns(temp, df = 4), ~ temp * PDO, etc. Per-species formulas. Register multiple specs parameter via linkages = list(log_K = list(spec_a, spec_b)) spec’s optional species = ... argument scoping subset stocks. pooler unions design columns across specs ’s duplication species share covariates. Priors. First-class via prior_normal(), prior_lognormal(), prior_gamma(), prior_beta(). constructors available unprefixed (normal() / lognormal() / …) inside priors = ... argument via private NSE data mask, user code stays close mathematical notation without masking base::gamma() / base::beta() package level. Priors can single value applied every species, named list keyed species id (shortly, (species, sex)). Bounds. Per-row lower / upper flow build_bounds()$lower$beta_linkage / build_bounds()$upper$beta_linkage. Growth (von Bertalanffy / Richards) first process fully wired new pipeline. build_growth() gains linkages argument string-named fun ("empirical" / "vonBertalanffy" / "Richards"); integer codes still work (fun = 1 shorthand fun = "vonBertalanffy") existing scripts don’t need rewritten apart substituting fun = growth_model =. TMB plumbing. New src/TMB/linkage.hpp accumulator; ceattle_v01_11.cpp reads parallel DATA_IVECTOR(linkage_*) inputs plus DATA_MATRIX(linkage_X) writes growth_linkage_offset tensor added (additively, log scale) growth_parameters. Per-row prior densities contribute slot 19 joint NLL (“Linkage-table priors” fit$quantities$jnll_comp). Documentation. New vignette vignette("environmental-linkages", package = "Rceattle") walks API, prior families, species-keyed priors, per-species formulas, basis-expansion formulas, underlying pipeline. Natural mortality second process wired pipeline. build_M1() gains linkages argument keyed log_M1; offset added log scale log_M1 inside M1_at_age compute. row’s age_bin == NA broadcasts offset across ages; specific values pin age slice. build_M1() also gains string-form acceptance M1_model M1_re (parity build_growth(fun)): Growth M can linked fit; rows share global linkage table beta_linkage parameter vector. Per-(species, sex) priors. addition scalar species-keyed priors, priors[[col]] value may two-level nested list keyed first species id sex id: Missing keys either level resolve “prior” stratum. validator checks structure recursively emits actionable error messages keyed priors$<col>$<species>[$<sex>] paths. Default = ~ species. linkage_spec() now defaults argument ~ species, linkage produces one coefficient per species without user spell . Pass ~ species + sex per-(species, sex) coefficients, = NULL share single coefficient across every species/sex (prior default). matches typical multispecies assessment use case stock environmental sensitivity. Recruitment third process wired pipeline. build_srr() gains linkages argument keyed log_R0, log_alpha, log_beta; offset added log scale corresponding parameter every recruitment compute call site (hindcast, BRPs, projections, expected R). log_R0 meaningful srr_fun; log_alpha log_beta work SRRs consume (srr_fun c(2, 3, 4, 5) – Beverton-Holt Ricker). Growth, M, recruitment can linked fit; rows share global linkage table beta_linkage parameter vector. End--end tests tests/testthat/tests-Dynamics/test-linkage-auto-map.R verify base parameter (e.g., log_growth_pars, log_M1, rec_pars) automatically mapped (set NA) linkage active parameter, allowing linkage intercept define base value. tests/testthat/tests-Dynamics/test-recruitment-linkage.R cover analytical relations R = R0 * exp(beta * temp[yr]) (mean R) growth + M + recruitment composition. Soft deprecation build_M1(). legacy column-index argument M1_indices env-driven structural integer codes M1_model %% c(4, 5) subsumed new linkages = list(log_M1 = ...) argument. still work one release cycle, emit one-time warning points users equivalent linkage-table call. string aliases "env_sex_invariant" / "env_sex_specific" (added briefly dev branch) removed; never released. cpp’s M1_beta / M1_mult code path stays place now – paths add additively log_M1 log scale – use coefficient double-count. Roadmap. Recruitment next pipeline; random-effects pooling re_group hierarchical shrinkage. legacy M1_indices / M1_model = 4|5 paths retire recruitment migrates.
code: build_growth(   fun = "vonBertalanffy",   linkages = list(     log_K = linkage_spec(       formula = ~ temp,       by      = ~ species + sex,       priors  = list(temp = normal(0, 1))     )   ) ) build_M1(M1_model = "sex_age_invariant",   # or 1          M1_re    = "ar1_age",             # or 4          linkages = list(            log_M1 = linkage_spec(formula = ~ temp, by = ~ species)          )) priors = list(   temp = list(     `1` = list(`1` = normal(0, 0.1),                `2` = normal(0, 0.2)),    # sp 1 by sex     `2` = normal(0, 0.5)                  # sp 2, both sexes   ) ) build_srr(   srr_fun  = 2,   linkages = list(     log_alpha = linkage_spec(formula = ~ temp,                              priors  = list(temp = normal(0, 0.5)))   ) )

title: Rceattle 4.0.1
text: Removed accumulation-age switches fleet_control. Selectivity normalization now controlled via Age_max_selected (.e. Sel_norm_bin1) per-fleet basis instead always normalizing maximum-selectivity age. NA values inside valid age/length range composition data now coerced 0 warning (previously silently dropped errored). Selectivity dimensioning switched age- bin-indexed non-parametric 2D/3D AR1 forms (driven Selectivity_dimension N_sel_bins). Age-error age-transition matrices now dimension-checked nages data_check() time.

title: Rceattle 4.0.0
text: CEATTLE TMB version 4.0.0. See Adams et al. (2022), Fisheries Research, 251, 106303.
